mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase by > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances following a sustained decline in RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from increased output and efficiency.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of instances following a INDPRO increase > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in > 40% of instances following the specified HOUST and UNRATE changes.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals disinflationary pressure, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate potential monetary easing and reduced cost pressures on businesses.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances following a CPIAUCSL decrease > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in > 40% of instances following the specified PAYEMS and UNRATE changes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending increase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances following a sustained increase in GDPC1.
